compiled_state.title: As a developer, cycle-ledger.json writes are serialized using the existing cross-platform locking primitive so they work on both macOS and Linux
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Description

**What**: Use the existing cross-platform locking library (Python fcntl-based, already used by suggestion-record.sh / ticket-lib-api.sh) for serializing concurrent cycle-ledger.json writes, replacing any direct `flock` binary call that would fail on macOS.
**Why**: macOS does not ship the flock(1) binary from util-linux. The plugin already has a cross-platform flock pattern that works on both macOS and Linux. Using it here ensures the cycle ledger introduced in the following story works for all contributors.
**Scope**:
- IN: Research and document which existing locking primitive in the plugin to reuse; define the cross-platform locking approach for S2; verify it works on macOS without Homebrew util-linux
- OUT: The cycle ledger itself (next story), the arbiter dispatch logic

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, the cross-platform locking approach for cycle-ledger.json is documented and references the existing plugin locking library (Python fcntl.flock wrapper), not the `flock` binary
  ← Satisfies: "Local merge strategy and PR merge strategy share identical arbiter input bundle structure and behavior" (SC3)
- When this story is complete, the locking approach has been verified to work on macOS without Homebrew util-linux installed
  ← Satisfies: SC3 (local/CI parity includes macOS contributor environments)
- When this story is complete, unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic

## Considerations

- [Reliability] The existing locking library in suggestion-record.sh uses Python fcntl — verify it is importable in the cycle-ledger write context before depending on it

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
